scope: Independent line-by-line verification of the published Hotspawn CS2 picks: the live inventory and every published probability, the executive summary's in-site pick links, the unresolved/limitations sections, and the phone layout of the six current pages.
method: The Arena sandbox has no egress to Hotspawn, HLTV, Polymarket, Kalshi or any esportsbook, so the live inventory and every live line were read on a GitHub runner with the publisher's own collector (session-only workflow .github/workflows/e5cc3d49-live.yml, deleted before merge). scripts/e5cc3d49_audit.py then re-derived every number it could from that row's own primary observation with no network access: Polymarket midpoints from the saved CLOB order books, esportsbook prices from the quoted decimal odds (1/o normalised), consensus rows from the per-provider median, and Valve-model rows from the published official points on the documented fixed-RD-75 Glicko scaling. Rows whose fit inputs are not in the published payload are named as not independently recomputable rather than marked verified. The built site was then checked for the executive summary's pick links, the complete-list anchors, the glance index (every active fixture and its published pick) and phone layout at 390 px. No probability, pick, alias or page was changed by this session.

items.finding: Every active Hotspawn CS2 fixture in the live inventory carries a published directional pick: 46 of 46 rows resolved, 0 unresolved, and the published method counts match the rows exactly (16 market, 8 bookmaker, 2 consensus, 20 model). No active fixture is missing from the complete list, and no row refers to a fixture outside the current inventory.
items.handling: Reconciled by scripts/e5cc3d49_audit.py against the live snapshot it read; the audit fails if any active fixture lacks a row, if any row is not in the inventory, or if the published counts disagree with the rows. The unresolved register therefore has no rows in this snapshot, and the executive summary states that explicitly. Run 39742089707 read the live snapshot of 2026-10-22T07:44Z and recorded the report in data/research/e5cc3d49/line-by-line-audit.json; the follow-up run 39744061339 on the corrected audit returned zero violations on the 07:56Z snapshot.

evidence.detail: Live complete list: every active fixture with both teams' probabilities, the pick and its evidence links.
Example official Hotspawn fixture page behind an audited row; every row links the fixture id it was harvested from.
The read-only audit that produced this register (coverage, counts, argmax, https-source and freshness checks).
The runner run that read the live Hotspawn inventory and every supported external line, then ran this audit against the freshly built site.

items.finding: 29 of the 46 published numbers were re-derived exactly from the primary observation quoted beside them: 16 Polymarket rows from the bid/ask the row publishes (and, where the collector saved the CLOB books, from those books' best bid and best ask), 8 esportsbook rows from their quoted decimal odds, 2 consensus rows from the median of their independent providers, and 3 Valve-model rows from the official published points. No row reproduced to a different value.
items.handling: Recomputation is arithmetic on the saved originals, with a 0.003 tolerance for the published rounding; a row that does not reproduce is reported as a violation, not smoothed. The remaining 17 model rows (Bradley–Terry network, HLTV-ranking and results-form fits) are published as not independently recomputable because their graph inputs are not part of the public payload; they are listed by fixture id and source in the audit report.

evidence.detail: The public payload this audit read: per-row method, probabilities, quotes, odds and official inputs.
Official Valve standings used both by the publisher's model rows and by this audit's re-derivation of them.
Example first-party market page: the moneyline shows g1 43c / tsa 58c, so a published 47.5/52.5 at 07:36Z is a point-in-time midpoint, not a claim about the current price.
The dated report: every row's checks, the 17 model rows that are not independently recomputable, and the exact violations found in that snapshot.

items.finding: The first version of this audit paired each published quote with the saved order book of the same position. That is wrong whenever Polymarket's outcome order differs from Hotspawn's team order (for example Polymarket lists 'Phantom Academy vs Falcons Force' while Hotspawn lists 'Falcons Force vs Phantom Academy'), because the collector reorders the quotes to the Hotspawn order. It produced four false 'does not reproduce' findings on fixtures 1081596 and 1082769.
items.handling: The audit now maps each team to its own book through the published source_outcomes and makes no book-level claim when the names cannot be mapped. Re-run on the live snapshot (run 39744061339): zero violations. The row itself was confirmed independently: Polymarket's own page for the Falcons Force–Phantom Academy series reports Falcons Force at 60c and Phantom Academy at 41c, which matches the published 59.5% / 40.5% midpoint. Locked by tests/test_e5cc3d49.py (reversed-outcome-order case).

evidence.detail: Polymarket's series moneyline for this fixture (Falcons Force 60c / Phantom Academy 41c) and its outcome order, which is the reverse of Hotspawn's.
The regression test that pins name-based book pairing.

items.finding: The repository's checked-in snapshot is still the 15 October collection (data/latest.json generated 2026-10-15T08:36:13Z, 80 records, 17 upcoming), while the live site serves the current runner snapshot. Because the platform still publishes this repository in legacy Pages build mode, every push to main briefly republishes those week-old root pages until the workflow's own artifact deploy lands.
items.handling: Not changed by this session: the root files are owned by the publisher and other live sessions. The publisher mitigates it by republishing its previous verified artifact first, and pages.yml re-reads the public snapshot after deployment. The underlying fix is a one-time Pages configuration change to 'GitHub Actions' as the source, which the repository's token cannot make (the configuration API answers HTTP 403). Flagged so the owner can switch it.

evidence.detail: The checked-in snapshot: generated_at 2026-10-15T08:36:13Z with 80 records, against the live site's 22 October snapshot.
The deployed snapshot served by the current artifact, which is what the executive summary renders.

items.finding: All six current pages are free of horizontal overflow at both 390 px and 320 px, carry the mobile viewport meta and a six-item bottom bar, and the executive summary reaches its pick index at 1,457 px (first pick row 1,751 px, about two phone screens). The exception is the Flagged for Review page: 116,265 px tall at 390 px and 137,397 px at 320 px, of which 112,452 px is the single 'All findings' register, where every finding is a full card. A phone reader must scroll roughly 130-160 screens to reach the end.
items.handling: Not changed here: the review page is built by scripts/build.py, which four other sessions were editing while this audit ran. Recommended fix, recorded for the owner: group the register by area behind a phone-first summary (counts per area plus a jump list) and keep the full cards inside per-area collapsible blocks, exactly as the dated earlier-session registers are already rendered. Raw measurements for /, /origination/, /picks/, /review/, /coverage/ and /methodology/ at both widths, including each tall section's height, are saved beside this register.

evidence.detail: The live register page this measurement describes.
390 px and 320 px measurements produced by this session on a local build of this branch, with per-page overflow, page height, pick-index offset and every section taller than 900 px.

items.finding: The complete-picks hero uses emoji as its only iconography (clipboard, flag, compass, link, books, target, house). Where the device has no emoji font the link text renders with a tofu box, and the emoji is part of the accessible name rather than hidden decoration.
items.handling: Not changed here: scripts/build_origination.py is outside this session's scope. Recommended fix: reuse the existing inline SVG icon set used by the sidebar and the executive summary, with aria-hidden on the icon. Every affected link still has a full text label, so nothing is unusable without the glyph.

evidence.detail: The hero whose quick links carry the emoji.

items.finding: The published-rank tie-break merged in PR #176 sets a pick direction on an exactly 50.0%/50.0% research-model estimate (fixture 1082926, Isurus vs Hacha, HLTV ranks 215 and 229). Three validators still required the opposite — 'an exactly even estimate must not name a pick' — and one of them is an assert inside the origination page builder. The first live snapshot containing such a fixture therefore aborted the publisher's build (originate check run 39748652200, 'AssertionError: Fallback pick differs from its probabilities'), which would fall the site back to the last verified snapshot.
items.handling: Fixed in this PR, narrowly: scripts/build_origination.py and scripts/coverage_audit.py (and this session's audit) now accept a side on an exactly even estimate only when the row publishes method='model', a tie_break record with a named rule and an https source, and a winner equal to the published pick; everything else still fails. The tie-break changes no probability, and it already adds its own explanation to the row's limitations and research trail, so the rendered card says why the pick exists. Pinned by tests/test_e5cc3d49.py::TieBreakTests (documented tie-break accepted by both audits, missing tie-break rejected, missing source rejected, winner mismatch rejected).

evidence.detail: The live originate check that failed with 'Fallback pick differs from its probabilities' after refetching first-party sources.
ranked_tie_break(): the documented rule — model rows only, exactly equal probabilities, two positive published ranks that differ, no probability changed.
The published ranking order the tie-break uses (fixture 1082926: Isurus 215, Hacha 229, equal points).

items.finding: tests/test_review_flags.py asserted that the published site/data/latest.json is byte-identical to data/latest.json. scripts/build.py::write_reconciled_snapshot (PR #176) deliberately adds three documented reconciliation keys to the published copy so the downloadable JSON cannot contradict the rendered page, so the assertion failed and blocked every pull request's test suite.
items.handling: Same defect, fixed upstream before this branch merged: session df80ab9f changed write_reconciled_snapshot() to publish the reconciliation in data/reconciled-counts.json, so data/latest.json is byte-identical again and the original assertion holds. This session briefly edited the test, then dropped that edit when the rebase showed the upstream fix; the register records the finding and the resolution, and no test change from this session remains in the tree.

evidence.detail: The pull-request run that failed on this assertion (annotation: 'FAIL: test_render_only_findings_do_not_rewrite_the_canonical_json') while the repository carried the keys-in-latest.json version.
write_reconciled_snapshot(): now writes data/reconciled-counts.json and leaves data/latest.json untouched, which is the contract the test asserts.
